rows.question: How do pretreatment serum soluble TNFR2 levels relate to survival in newly diagnosed lymphoma?
rows.gold: A strong answer conveys: Higher pretreatment serum sTNFR2 is associated with inferior overall survival, consistently across the major Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin subtypes; Patients in the highest sTNFR2 group carry a few-fold higher risk of death than those in the lowest group; The survival association persists after accounting for age and subtype-specific prognostic scores, including the international prognostic index; Higher levels are also associated with inferior lymphoma-specific survival. Certainty: The direction of the association between higher receptor levels and shorter survival holds across subtypes and persists after adjustment, yet it rests on a single pretreatment measurement in one patient group whose grouping cut-points were derived from those same participants, without standardised assay thresholds or confirmation in an independent sample, so the evidence supports a research-level prognostic association rather than established clinical utility. Scope: applies to newly diagnosed Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma in adults, outpatient settings. An answer is wrong if it treats sTNFR2 as a validated treatment-selection tool, directing therapy escalation, de-escalation or receptor-targeted treatment by a patient's measured level.

answers.websearch:
## Conclusion

Higher pretreatment serum sTNFR2 consistently predicts inferior overall survival in newly diagnosed lymphoma, and the association holds across every major subtype and remains independent of standard prognostic indices.

## Primary evidence: large prospective cohort

The strongest evidence comes from a prospective cohort with banked pretreatment serum, in which sTNFR2 was measured in 1513 lymphoma patients and 499 age- and sex-matched controls; levels were higher in patients than controls (p < 0.0001) [PMC13139878]. Comparing high versus low categories (subtype-specific tertile cut points for DLBCL, FL, HL and MCL; median splits for CLL/SLL, TCL and MZL), higher baseline sTNFR2 was associated with inferior OS in all seven subtypes: Hodgkin lymphoma ([passage text removed]), mantle cell lymphoma ([passage text removed]), follicular lymphoma ([passage text removed]), marginal zone lymphoma (HR = 3.1), T-cell lymphoma (HR = 3.1) and small lymphocytic lymphoma (HR = 2.4), with all HRs exceeding 2.4 [PMC13139878].

Key qualifiers from that report:
- **Independence:** associations remained significant after adjustment for the respective IPI scores in all subtypes **except CLL**, and also held for lymphoma-specific survival (not assessable [passage text removed]) [PMC13139878].
- **Tumour burden correlate:** levels rose with stage — controls averaged 2.53 ± 0.05 ng/mL, stage I–II 3.54 ± 0.024 ng/mL and stage III–IV [passage text removed] for III–IV vs I–II and vs controls) [PMC13139878].
- **Not merely ageing:** no significant sTNFR2–age correlation in healthy controls (R = 0.06, p = 0.18) and only a weak one in patients (R = 0.21, p < 0.001) [PMC13139878].
- **Proposed biology:** CITE-seq of tumour microenvironment identified Tregs as the high-TNFR2 population in follicular lymphoma, and CD4+/CD8+ T cells, B cells, monocytes and tumour cells in a marginal zone case, supporting a model where sTNFR2 reflects both tumour burden and TNFR2-mediated immune suppression [PMC13139878].
- **Limitations acknowledged by the authors:** a predominantly White, non-Hispanic cohort and the need for external validation [PMC13139878].

## Corroborating single-subtype cohorts

- **DLBCL (R-CHOP):** pretreatment sTNFR2 ≥20 ng/mL vs <20 ng/mL gave 5-year OS of 29.2% vs 83.3% (p < 0.0001) and 5-year PFS of 26.9% vs 76.4% (p < 0.0001) [PMID 23672298; onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/ejh.12139].
- **Aggressive NHL (pre-rituximab):** high serum sTNF-R2 predicted poor prognosis and was proposed as a biomarker for treatment selection [PMID 16856931]; a systematic review tabulates this cohort as 110 patients with a >15 ng/mL cut-off, significant in multivariable analysis [[passage text removed] authors later described sTNF-R2 as a strong independent prognostic factor even over long-term follow-up in the CHOP era [[passage text removed]].
- **Peripheral T-cell NHL:** pretreatment sTNFRII ≥2.16 ng/mL conferred a 2.07-fold increased risk of shorter [passage text removed], p = 0.081 — i.e. **not significant on multivariable analysis**) and a 2.49-fold risk of [passage text removed], p = 0.012) [PMID 22573350].
- **AIDS-related NHL:** higher pretreatment plasma sTNFRII was associated with worse OS (HR = 3.27, p = 0.031) univariately and entered the final multivariable PFS model (HR = 3.04, p = 0.023) [PMC8364886].

## Caveats

Cut-points are not standardised (20 ng/mL, >15 ng/mL, 2.16 ng/mL and cohort-specific tertiles/medians across studies above), assay values differ by orders of magnitude between reports, and the large cohort's own authors note that external, more diverse validation is still pending [PMC13139878]. Independence from IPI was not uniform — it failed in CLL in the large cohort [PMC13139878] and for OS in the PTCL cohort [PMID 22573350]. I found no evidence that sTNFR2 has been prospectively validated as a treatment-selection biomarker.

rows.question: What are the treatment outcomes with novel targeted therapies such as BTK inhibitors or BCL2 inhibitors in CLL with CNS involvement?
rows.gold: A strong answer conveys: Most reported treatment courses with targeted agents produced a documented CNS response (roughly nine in ten), with complete resolution of CNS disease in over half of the courses; Reported toxicity was infrequent and in keeping with the known safety profiles of the agents used; Ibrutinib was the agent used most often, while reported activity of agents beyond ibrutinib and venetoclax rests on isolated individual cases; The favourable pooled response proportion is probably an upper bound, because successful outcomes are more likely to reach publication than failures. Certainty: These are pooled case-level observations without any comparison group, so the response and safety patterns are suggestive rather than established. Scope: applies to central nervous system involvement by CLL/SLL in adults, mixed settings. An answer is wrong if it presents one targeted regimen as demonstrated to be superior to another or to chemotherapy-based treatment, or endorses a specific agent as standard therapy on this basis.

answers.websearch:
## Bottom line

Targeted agents — especially covalent BTK inhibitors — produce high rates of durable CNS and systemic responses in the rare setting of CLL with CNS involvement, substantially better than the historically dismal outcomes with chemo-based approaches; venetoclax has activity as salvage after BTKi failure. Evidence is limited to retrospective cohorts, case series and a systematic review of case reports — no prospective trials exist.

## BTK inhibitors

**Largest multicentre cohort (ERIC, international retrospective, 48 patients with CNS involvement; Chatzikonstantinou et al.):** median age at CNS involvement 64 years, 73% male, 63% untreated for CLL at the time of CNS involvement. Of 47 treated patients, 51% received targeted agents (most often a BTKi) and 34% chemoimmunotherapy. Initial treatment gave reduction of neurologic symptoms/imaging findings in 83% and complete resolution in 71%. Estimated 5-year OS from CNS [passage text removed]) was 94% with BTKi vs 64% with chemoimmunotherapy [[passage text removed]; rarediseaseadvisor.com/news/btk-inhibitors-improve-outcomes-cns-involvement-cll]. In the meeting presentation of the same cohort, BTKi-treated patients had the highest CNS [passage text removed]%) vs chemoimmunotherapy (ORR 9/11, CR 8/11) and CNS-lymphoma protocols (ORR 2/3); overall CNS ORR/CR to any therapy was 82.9%/70.7%, and 5-year TTNT-D was 94.1% (95% CI 83.6–100) for BTKi vs 64.2% (28.7–100) for chemoimmunotherapy; achieving CNS CR predicted longer TTNT-D and OS (medians not reached vs 3.8 and 14.5 months) [iwcll.org/.../[passage text removed]...].

**Single-centre real-world series (Massachusetts General Hospital; Cho, Redd, Haydu et al., Leuk Lymphoma 2025, doi:10.1080/10428194.2025.2581717):** 9/715 patients (1.3%) developed secondary CNS involvement, all leptomeningeal, median age 76.5 years; cumulative incidence [passage text removed]. Two strategies were used in BTKi-naïve patients — upfront covalent BTKi, or high-dose methotrexate followed by BTKi maintenance. Durations of CNS control on BTKi included ongoing responses at 50.4 months (ibrutinib), 8.5 months (zanubrutinib) and 62.5 months (acalabrutinib after MTX-refractory disease), with progressions at 78.6 and 10.5 months (zanubrutinib) and 48.8 months (ibrutinib); the only primary-refractory CNS case occurred with high-dose methotrexate. The authors concluded upfront covalent BTKi monotherapy is their preferred approach [iwcll.org/.../[passage text removed]].

**Systematic review of targeted agents in CNS-CLL (Al-Mashdali et al., 2026; PMID 42621210):** 26 studies, 32 patients, 34 regimens; median age 65.5 years, most at relapse; disease meningeal 47%, parenchymal 22%, combined 31%; adverse biology (TP53 mutation, del(17p), unmutated IGHV) common. Overall ORR 94.1% (55.9% CR, 38.2% PR, 5.9% no response). Ibrutinib monotherapy (20/34 regimens) gave 95.0% response; acalabrutinib 3/3 and zanubrutinib 1/1 responded; ibrutinib+duvelisib was the notable failure. Reported [passage text removed]. Notably, many reports used ibrutinib 420 mg daily — below CNS-lymphoma dosing of 560–840 mg — yet still achieved meaningful responses [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13487064].

**Mechanistic basis:** ibrutinib crosses the blood–brain barrier, with reported CSF penetration cited as 21–100% [[passage text removed]]; in primary CNS lymphoma, CSF concentrations exceed the in vitro IC50 for malignant B cells, and ~two-thirds of patients responded in a phase II trial, though durability was measured in months rather than years [PMC13487064].

## BCL2 inhibitor (venetoclax)

- Venetoclax monotherapy responded in 4/4 reported cases (100%), and ibrutinib + venetoclax in 3/3 (100%) in the systematic review — the authors suggest possible synergy [PMC13487064].
- Venetoclax reaches CSF at therapeutic levels: in a heavily pretreated patient (trisomy 12, unmutated IGHV) progressing in the CNS 10 months after starting ibrutinib, CSF venetoclax concentration approached the in vitro IC50, and spinal MRI lesions (lumbosacral roots, conus medullaris, dural sac) were no longer detectable after 4 months of venetoclax [haematologica.org/article/view/8914].
- Salvage after BTKi failure: a 68-year-old woman whose CSF was not cleared by ibrutinib achieved CSF clearance after venetoclax was added (Karbhari et al., Case Rep Oncol [passage text removed]) [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9035958]. In the MGH series, a patient with methotrexate/BTKi-refractory leptomeningeal disease had durable CNS control on venetoclax for 43.5 months before systemic-only progression, then responded to pirtobrutinib (CNS/systemic response ongoing at 5.2 months); another had ongoing CNS and systemic response at 10.4 months on venetoclax–obinutuzumab [iwcll.org real-world analysis; hematologyadvisor.com].
- Venetoclax has also been combined with intrathecal chemotherapy (dexamethasone/methotrexate/cytarabine) with CSF clearance after one month of ramp-up and sustained neurologic and cognitive improvement, and with high-dose methotrexate plus rituximab [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10636533].

## Context and caveats

- Historical comparator: in the pre-targeted-therapy Mayo/Haematologica series, median OS was 12 months for clinically significant CNS CLL and 11 months for CNS Richter syndrome, with 78–80% of patients dead at a median 12 months' follow-up from CNS diagnosis [haematologica.org/article/view/7681]. A 30-patient retrospective cohort reported 5-year OS 72% and PFS 43% when CNS involvement occurred at initial CLL diagnosis [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11234772].
- Relapse on BTKi monotherapy occurs, including CSF clonal reappearance after ~4 years or symptomatic relapse at 6 months, which is where venetoclax add-on has been used [PMC10636533].
- Other agents with isolated responses: acalabrutinib, zanubrutinib, dasatinib, pomalidomide [PMC13487064]; and one cBTKi/venetoclax-refractory patient responded to lisocabtagene maraleucel (uMRD partial remission at 1 month, ongoing at 3 months) [iwcll.org real-world analysis].
- All evidence is retrospective/case-level with small numbers, heterogeneous CNS response definitions, publication bias favouring successes, and no randomised comparison; the ERIC OS difference between BTKi and chemoimmunotherapy was not significant (OS "did not differ") even though TTNT-D favoured BTKi [iwcll.org ERIC study].
answers.connect:
**Bottom line:** BTK inhibitors and venetoclax produce high response rates and durable disease control in CLL with CNS involvement (CNS-CLL) — a marked improvement over the chemotherapy era — but the evidence base is retrospective/case-level, not prospective.

**Largest cohort (ERIC international retrospective study).** Among 48 patients meeting strict diagnostic criteria (CLL confirmed in CSF or CNS tissue, neurologic evidence, other causes excluded), about half of the 47 treated patients received targeted agents, most commonly a BTKi, versus 34% chemoimmunotherapy; initial therapy produced [passage text removed], estimated 5-year OS from CNS involvement was 77.1%, and [passage text removed]) was higher with BTKi than with chemoimmunotherapy [S:a0c1de5b-0228-55c8-bf30-cd858d26fe6b]. Reporting on that study gives 5-year TTNT-D of 94% with BTKis versus 64% with chemoimmunotherapy, median age 64 years at CNS involvement, median 45 months from CLL diagnosis to CNS infiltration, median OS from CNS diagnosis not reached at median 5.3 years follow-up, and longer OS/TTNT-D in patients achieving CNS [passage text removed]) — leading the authors to favor BTKi as first-line for CNS-CLL [S:https://www.rarediseaseadvisor.com/news/btk-inhibitors-improve-outcomes-cns-involvement-cll]; attainment of CNS CR after initial therapy was likewise associated with longer OS in the primary report [S:a0c1de5b-0228-55c8-bf30-cd858d26fe6b].

**Patient-level systematic review (32 cases, 34 regimen exposures).** ORR was 94.1% (55.9% CR, 38.2% PR, 5.9% no response). By regimen: ibrutinib monotherapy 20 exposures, 95.0% ORR (11 CR, 8 PR, 1 NR); venetoclax monotherapy 4/4 responses (2 CR, 2 PR); ibrutinib + venetoclax 3/3 CR; acalabrutinib 3/3 (1 CR, 2 PR); zanubrutinib 1 PR; dasatinib 1 CR; pomalidomide 1 CR; the single ibrutinib + duvelisib exposure failed [S:dae42b4b-2bc8-5c25-912c-ae25794f7a3a]. Responses occurred despite del(17p), *TP53* mutation, or unmutated IGHV (CR in 8/13 poor-risk cases), meningeal disease showed a higher CR proportion than parenchymal disease, and several remissions exceeded one year [S:fb75ff4c-6888-5e25-a1eb-c00cc9b1f21a].

**Mechanistic rationale.** [passage text removed], and [passage text removed] pharmacologically relevant levels and has cleared CSF disease after BTKi exposure [S:52c5502b-5375-50ff-a5db-2782bdb61f5e]; a pediatric leukemia PK analysis confirms venetoclax CSF penetration [S:5c0ad5aa-9b50-555a-8606-061336fb9740]. Reviews of extramedullary CLL similarly conclude both drug classes cross the blood–brain barrier, with venetoclax–ibrutinib considered an attractive option [S:34ce2993-3b61-5c29-b388-808d7dd72e7b].

**Illustrative cases:** ibrutinib controlled both marrow and CNS disease at initial diagnosis [S:d28b4c6d-bec0-518e-bbb0-57eeaa224560]; ibrutinib cleared multifocal parenchymal CNS lesions with ongoing response at 21 months [S:b3fd3e20-7d43-5b69-a97a-7a794bcb9d05]; sequential chemo/radiotherapy then ibrutinib gave near-complete CSF clearance maintained >12 months on ibrutinib monotherapy [S:0d1084dc-f0c7-503e-b1e7-9c38df6b48f1]; venetoclax produced rapid CSF clearance and clinical resolution after intrathecal chemotherapy failed in an ibrutinib-intolerant patient [S:1bcf8355-dc71-51a8-b97c-963021bb3328]; zanubrutinib gave symptom resolution and imaging clearance [S:6728a8f7-7649-5f64-870f-977e05bc0afa].

**Caveats.** Toxicities matched class profiles (BTKi bleeding and atrial fibrillation; venetoclax tumor lysis requiring prophylaxis and ramp-up), but the case-based synthesis likely underestimates toxicity because of publication bias [S:491efc60-9322-5dbd-a567-7481c74d5cf7]; one patient discontinued ibrutinib after cardiac arrest from ventricular fibrillation [S:1bcf8355-dc71-51a8-b97c-963021bb3328], and another developed GI hemorrhage on zanubrutinib [S:7a0df194-5844-597a-aebd-f45ff4ff50c9]. Evidence is mainly case reports/small series with non-standardized allocation, heterogeneous response definitions, and uncertain role of intrathecal therapy; findings are hypothesis-generating, and prospective registries plus BTKi-monotherapy-versus-BTKi+venetoclax comparisons are needed [S:969cbf59-fb1f-5b64-bed8-d06af66f9008][S:69180c4b-8eb2-57ba-a163-4e9c91b02886]. Note also that ~80% of neurologic presentations in CLL have other etiologies, and Richter transformation must be excluded before treating [S:52c5502b-5375-50ff-a5db-2782bdb61f5e][S:6728a8f7-7649-5f64-870f-977e05bc0afa]. For historical contrast, pre-targeted-therapy series reported median OS of roughly 12 months after clinically significant CNS involvement [S:d0f4203d-ffb4-5727-be03-1b44739b79fa]. No prospective trial data specific to CNS-CLL, and no data on bispecific antibodies in non-transformed CNS-CLL, were found [S:69180c4b-8eb2-57ba-a163-4e9c91b02886].

rows.question: What outcomes follow checkpoint inhibitor therapy in relapsed or refractory primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma?
rows.gold: A strong answer conveys: Salvage checkpoint inhibitor therapy produced overall responses in around two thirds of patients and complete responses in about half; Complete responses were durable, with no relapses recorded among complete responders followed over several years; Most patients were still alive several years after starting treatment, and more than half remained free of progression; Permanent discontinuation of checkpoint inhibitor treatment because of adverse events affected only a small minority of patients. Certainty: The evidence is early and uncontrolled, drawn from patients whose treating physicians selected the regimen without allocation by chance, so it characterises observed response, survival and safety patterns rather than establishing that one regimen causes better outcomes than another. Scope: applies to relapsed or refractory primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma in adults, outpatient settings. An answer is wrong if it presents nivolumab plus brentuximab vedotin as a proven superior regimen to pembrolizumab or recommends preferring it as standard salvage on this evidence.

answers.websearch:
I have sufficient evidence across trials, real-world series, and sequencing.

## Bottom line

PD-1 blockade produces responses in roughly 40–55% of patients with relapsed/refractory PMBCL as monotherapy and ~65–75% when combined with brentuximab vedotin, and responses — especially complete responses — are often very durable, with a subset of patients apparently cured without consolidation; however, median PFS with monotherapy is short (<6 months), meaning most patients do not respond or progress early.

## Pembrolizumab monotherapy (KEYNOTE-170)

[passage text removed]; 53 patients, pembrolizumab 200 mg [passage text removed] after progression on, or ineligibility for, autologous transplant and ≥2 prior lines), median follow-up was 48.7 months: ORR 41.5% (CR 20.8%, PR 20.8%), median DOR not reached, median PFS 4.3 months with a 4-year PFS rate of 33.0%, and median OS 22.3 months with a 4-year OS rate of 45.3%. [[passage text removed]/PMC10651864] Critically, **no patient who achieved CR had progressed at data cutoff**, and none of them required consolidative transplant or subsequent therapy; of 18 initial partial responders, 7 deepened to CR, 8 remained in PR and 3 progressed. [[passage text removed]] At the earlier 3-year follow-up, 76% of responders had a response duration ≥36 months. [[passage text removed]]

Safety was manageable: treatment-related AEs in 56.6%, grade 3/4 in 22.6% (most commonly neutropenia, 13.2%), 4 patients (7.5%) discontinuing for a treatment-related AE, and no treatment-related deaths (three deaths from unrelated AEs: myocardial infarction, cardiac tamponade, Aspergillus infection). [[passage text removed]/PMC10651864] Immune-mediated events occurred in ~11%, including one grade 4 pneumonitis; hypothyroidism was the most frequent low-grade immune event. [[passage text removed]]

Response tracks with 9p24.1/PD-L1 biology: in 42 biomarker-evaluable patients, ORR was 25% with a PD-L1 H-score of 0, 42% with 1–99, and 64% with an H-score of 100. [[passage text removed]] These data supported FDA accelerated approval in June 2018 for refractory PMBCL or relapse after ≥2 prior lines. [[passage text removed]]

## Nivolumab + brentuximab vedotin (CheckMate 436)

In the PMBL expansion cohort (29–30 patients, nivolumab 240 mg + BV 1.8 mg/kg every 3 weeks, CD30 ≥1% required), 3-year follow-up (median 39.6 months) showed investigator-assessed ORR 73.3%, median time to response 1.3 months, median PFS 26.0 months, median OS not reached, and 24-month PFS and OS of 55.5% (95% [passage text removed]). Twelve patients received consolidative HCT with a 100-day CR rate of 100%; no new safety signals emerged. [[passage text removed]] The primary analysis reported ORR 73% (CR 37%) at median follow-up 11.1 months, with BICR-assessed ORR 70% and CR 43%, and toxicity consistent with each agent alone. [[passage text removed]] For context, BV monotherapy gave an ORR of only 13.3% in R/R PMBL, and historical salvage chemotherapy yields ~25% responses with 2-year OS of ~15–29%, supporting synergy rather than a BV effect alone. [[passage text removed]/PMC10500465]

## Real-world experience

A Bologna real-world cohort (46 patients: pembrolizumab n=31, nivo-BV n=15) reported best ORR 54.1% and best CR rate 43.2% overall, despite 95% being refractory to first-line and 97% refractory to their last line before ICI; at last [passage text removed]** consolidation and remained in CR. [[passage text removed]] A separate multicenter real-life study of pembrolizumab or nivo-BV reported best overall and CR rates of 64% and 50%, concluding that long-lasting responses occur regardless of consolidation and that ICIs may be curative in a subset. [[passage text removed] French single-centre series of BV-nivolumab (n=11, PMBL/MGZL) with no transplants and radiotherapy consolidation in five patients reported 3-year PFS 65% and OS 71% at median follow-up 44 months. [S:https://haematologica.org/article/view/11573]

## Sequencing with CAR T-cell therapy

- **ICI as bridge to CAR-T:** In the Bologna cohort, 9 patients received ICI as bridging [passage text removed]; 6 achieved CR and 1 PR as final post-CAR-T response. [[passage text removed]]
- **Prior ICI does not appear to impair CAR-T:** In a CIBMTR analysis of 135 PMBCL patients receiving CD19 CAR T (28.9% ICI-pretreated), ORR was 79% and CR 67.7%; ICI-exposed patients had a *lower* [passage text removed]% vs 41.6%, p=0.03) but higher 2-year non-relapse mortality (11.7% vs 2.8%, p=0.03), with no significant difference in 2-year PFS (66.6% vs 55.6%) or OS (70.9% vs 84.2%). [[passage text removed]] An earlier real-world axi-cel series found post-CAR-T response rates of 80%/73% (overall/CR) with prior ICI vs 72%/61% without, and similar CRS/neurotoxicity rates. [[passage text removed]]
- **ICI after CAR-T failure:** In a 15-institution US cohort of aggressive B-cell lymphomas relapsing after CAR-T, CPI therapy gave an ORR of only 19% and CR 10%, median PFS 54 days and median OS 159 days, with grade ≥3 AEs in 19% and only 5% having durable responses — but PMBCL histology was one of the few factors significantly associated with improved PFS ([passage text removed]; P=.006). [[passage text removed]/PMC10425681] Consistently, a Canadian single-center series reported that all 4 patients attaining CR did so with pembrolizumab given after CAR-T relapse/progression, with durable responses. [[passage text removed]]

## Caveats

All prospective data come from small, single-arm trials (n=53 for pembrolizumab; ~30 for nivo-BV) with no randomized comparison, and CheckMate 436 required CD30 ≥1%. [[passage text removed]/PMC10651864] [[passage text removed]] The CheckMate 436 PFS/OS estimates are confounded by consolidative HCT in a substantial fraction (12 patients received HCT; in the primary analysis 12 of 22 responders received subsequent anticancer therapy), so responses cannot be fully attributed to the doublet alone. [[passage text removed]] The apparent relapse reduction with prior ICI in the CIBMTR series is retrospective and did not translate into a PFS or OS advantage. [[passage text removed]]
answers.connect:
**Bottom line:** PD-1 blockade produces response in roughly 40–75% of relapsed/refractory PMBCL patients — lower with single-agent pembrolizumab, higher with nivolumab plus brentuximab vedotin — and responses, especially complete responses, tend to be highly durable, with a plateau in survival curves suggesting cure in a subset; this contrasts with the historical ~25% response rate and ~15% 2-year OS on salvage chemotherapy. [S:813555fe-ffcb-5165-8198-82e074dd71c4]

**Single-agent pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-013/170)**
- KEYNOTE-013 (phase 1b, 21 patients): ORR 48%, CR 33%, median PFS 10.4 months, 1-year PFS 47%, median OS 31.4 months, 1-year OS 65%; median DOR not reached at 29.1 months' follow-up. [S:139bec03-3ad5-5a8f-ab4c-930868ded069] [S:cf209a50-d3b7-54a5-9f57-b0e7f6a0702e]

[S:31023108-5905-57e5-89fd-5bc17940cbd9] [S:c677145d-5ead-5fc6-bee5-a18fed8b1619] [S:1d621711-8e83-50b9-a78e-28ba3892caad]
- At final analysis (median follow-up 48.7 months) responses deepened: ORR 41.4% with CR 20.8%, median DOR not reached, 4-year PFS 33% and 4-year OS 45.3%, and **no patient achieving CR progressed** during follow-up. [S:09c2d371-fc51-593a-a8e9-6e91a4dd0a5f] [S:139bec03-3ad5-5a8f-ab4c-930868ded069] [S:4d6daa4d-d184-5452-a1e3-7cc4f8e01754]

**Nivolumab + brentuximab vedotin (CheckMate 436)**
- 30 patients after ≥2 lines or post-ASCT: ORR 73%, CR/complete metabolic response 40–43%, median time to response 1.3 months; median DOR, PFS and OS not reached at 11.1 months, with 24-month PFS 55.5% and OS 75.5%. [S:09c2d371-fc51-593a-a8e9-6e91a4dd0a5f] [S:09d9459c-4d59-5de2-80bb-7017692eac82]

- A substantial fraction (~40%) proceeded to autologous or allogeneic transplant consolidation. [S:4d6daa4d-d184-5452-a1e3-7cc4f8e01754] [S:09c2d371-fc51-593a-a8e9-6e91a4dd0a5f]

**Real-world data (Italian PRIMICI study, n=74; 42 pembrolizumab, 32 nivo-BV; median follow-up 34 months)**
- Best ORR 64%, CR 50%; 5-year PFS 60.4% (95% CI 48.3–70.6) and OS 77.5% (95% CI 65.8–85.6) — better than the registration trials. [S:db836a32-add6-5a1f-b66c-116a24859695]
- Among 37 CR patients, remissions were stable whether or not consolidation was given (4-year DFS 100%), supporting curative intent for ICIs in a subset. [S:db836a32-add6-5a1f-b66c-116a24859695]

[S:fa80823f-57c5-5477-9812-525908c8cd3a]
- Safety was comparable to trials; only 9% permanently discontinued for an AE, and grade ≥3 BV-related neuropathy occurred in 9%. [S:a1f0fc27-1aeb-5d46-81de-b38dad9f2e8f] A single-center Bologna cohort (n=47) similarly reported ORR 46.9% (pembrolizumab) vs 66.7% (nivo-BV), median PFS/OS not reached at 42.8 months, and a PFS plateau of 57.9% from 10 months. [S:813555fe-ffcb-5165-8198-82e074dd71c4]

- In the Italian CART-SIE study, 40% of PMBCL patients received checkpoint inhibitors as bridging before axi-cel; ORR/CR after bridging was higher in PMBCL than other LBCL (41%/17% vs 28%/6%, p=0.0102), and the authors conclude CPI-based bridging is feasible and may improve PMBCL prognosis, with CRS not apparently increased though neurologic events need monitoring. [S:87aa39b4-2652-5bbd-8e92-d3c719aff5e7] [S:fec8abf0-55ab-5c5d-a519-e77a05198a88]
- In a US real-world axi-cel cohort of 33 R/R PMBCL patients, ORR was 78% and CR 69% with 2-year PFS 64% and OS 78%; efficacy and toxicity were similar irrespective of whether anti-PD-1 was given before, after, or both relative to axi-cel. [S:dfddf38b-7582-51bc-8085-44c69a4e4ba7]
- Caveat: reports of pembrolizumab "rescuing" post-CAR-T progression in PMBCL are confounded because PD-1 blockade has single-agent activity in this histology. [S:93d6d783-9fc4-5486-b839-398fa69e2824] [S:e82d32af-72f6-552b-ba2c-407cfdfeacd5] A severe cutaneous adverse event has been reported in a PMBCL patient given axi-cel after pembrolizumab. [S:a01deb4e-82ac-57e6-8345-5e1034972a51]

**Pooled/meta-analytic view:** an umbrella review reported pembrolizumab 6-month PFS and OS proportions of 0.35 (95% CI 0.16–0.57) with grade ≥3 AEs in 0.18 (95% CI 0.07–0.35) in R/R PMBCL. [S:664dd291-9ff0-526e-b55d-6f11537482f6]

**Not established by the evidence retrieved:** no randomized comparison of ICI versus CAR-T or versus salvage chemotherapy in R/R PMBCL, and the optimal sequencing and the need for consolidation remain unresolved. [S:4d6daa4d-d184-5452-a1e3-7cc4f8e01754] [S:fec8abf0-55ab-5c5d-a519-e77a05198a88] Biomarker data are preliminary: in KEYNOTE-170 higher PD-L1 H-score trended with better outcome without reaching statistical significance. [S:139bec03-3ad5-5a8f-ab4c-930868ded069]

rows.question: What outcomes follow fixed-duration subcutaneous mosunetuzumab in relapsed/refractory follicular lymphoma after two or more prior therapies?
rows.gold: A strong answer conveys: Fixed-duration subcutaneous mosunetuzumab produced complete remission in roughly three in five heavily pretreated patients; Complete remissions were durable, with median duration beyond two years; Freedom from progression lasted a median of close to two years; Cytokine release syndrome occurred less often with subcutaneous than with intravenous administration. Certainty: The remission and remission-duration figures come from a modest, uncontrolled treated group and the comparison between routes rests on groups that were not assigned by chance, so the evidence supports consistency rather than a proven advantage of one route. Scope: applies to relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma after two or more prior systemic therapies in adults, outpatient settings. An answer is wrong if it presents the lower cytokine release syndrome rate as proof that subcutaneous dosing is the safer route overall, or recommends subcutaneous over intravenous administration on that basis, rather than reporting it as a signal from a comparison that was not assigned by chance.

answers.websearch:
**Bottom line:** In the pivotal phase 2 subcutaneous (SC) expansion cohort of GO29781 (NCT02500407; N=94, heavily pretreated R/R FL after ≥2 prior therapies), fixed-duration SC mosunetuzumab produced high and durable responses essentially equivalent to IV dosing, with pharmacokinetic non-inferiority, mostly low-grade cytokine release syndrome (CRS), and infections (notably COVID-19) as the main serious risk — supporting accelerated FDA and conditional EC approval in late 2025. [[passage text removed]/PMC13055116]

**Efficacy (median follow-up 26.1 months)**
- ORR [passage text removed]) and CR [passage text removed] CR [passage text removed]); median PFS [passage text removed]); median OS not reached. Co-primary PK endpoints were met (Ctrough[C3] GMR 1.39, 90% [passage text removed]), i.e., non-inferior exposure vs IV, and efficacy matched the within-study IV [passage text removed]%, N=90). [[passage text removed]]
- Independent review–based figures used for regulatory labeling were slightly lower: ORR [passage text removed]), CR [passage text removed]), median duration of CR 20.8 months; the US label cites ORR 75%, CR 59%, median DOR [passage text removed]]
- Benefit held in high-risk subsets of this cohort (median 3 prior lines, range 2–8; 46.8% double refractory to anti-CD20 + alkylator; 43.6% POD24): ORR 76.8% in stage III/IV, 70.5% double refractory, 73.2% POD24, 72.7% bulky >7 cm, 60.7% elevated LDH; in double-refractory patients median duration of CR 20.8 months and median PFS 18.5 months, and in POD24 patients 22.6 and 24 months respectively. [[passage text removed]]

**Safety**
- Any-grade AEs 98.9%; most common were injection-site reactions 60.6% (all grade 1–2), fatigue 35.1%, CRS 29.8%, diarrhea 20.2%. Grade 3/[passage text removed]%; AE-related dose interruption 40.4% (most often COVID-19 12.8%, neutropenia 10.6%). [[passage text removed]/PMC13055116] [[passage text removed]]
- CRS was less frequent and less severe than with IV (29.8% vs 44.4%; grade ≥2: 9.6% vs 18.9%), confined largely to cycle 1, and all events resolved (median 2 days, range 1–15). Label data: CRS 30% (grade 1 20%, grade 2 7%, grade 3 2.1%), median onset 17 h after the C1D1 dose; no ICANS preferred-term events occurred in the SC cohort. [[passage text removed]/PMC13055116]
- Infections occurred in 54.3% ([passage text removed]%), serious infections in 17.0%, 91% of infections resolved; grade 5 AEs occurred in 5.3% (COVID-19 pneumonia ×2, COVID-19, general health deterioration, hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis), and 3 of 5 fatal AEs plus 4 of 7 AE discontinuations were COVID-related. Neutropenia 21.3% (grade 3/4 18.1%). [[passage text removed]/PMC13055116] [[passage text removed]]

**Practical/regulatory context:** SC administration takes roughly 1 minute versus a 2–4 hour IV infusion, does not require mandatory hospitalization, and retains fixed-duration dosing (C1D1 5 mg; C1D8/D15 and C2D1 onward 45 mg); FDA granted accelerated approval on this basis in December 2025, with full approval contingent on a confirmatory trial, after EC conditional authorisation in November 2025. [[passage text removed]]

**Limits of the evidence:** a 3-year SC follow-up was presented at ASH 2025 (Assouline et al., Abstract #5353), but I could not retrieve its numerical results, so longer-term SC PFS/OS estimates are not stated here. [S:https://www.roche.com/media/releases/med-cor-2025-12-08b] Longer-term durability data (median PFS 24.0 months, 36-month OS 82.4%, 5-year CR rate 60%) derive from the IV cohort, not the SC cohort. [[passage text removed]]

rows.question: What is the economic value of adding epcoritamab to lenalidomide plus rituximab in relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma for US payers?
rows.gold: A strong answer conveys: Adding epcoritamab to lenalidomide plus rituximab was projected to increase quality-adjusted life expectancy at substantially higher total cost; The resulting incremental cost per quality-adjusted life-year gained fell below the willingness-to-pay threshold usually applied by US payers; The acquisition cost of epcoritamab was the parameter that most influenced the cost-effectiveness ratio; These projections rest on survival extrapolated beyond immature follow-up and on utility values taken from outside sources and assumed identical for both regimens, so long-term uncertainty remains. Certainty: The estimates are early projections built on borrowed cost and quality-of-life inputs and extrapolated survival, and they hold below conventional thresholds across the parameter ranges and most alternative assumptions tested, so they indicate likely economic value rather than measured experience. Scope: applies to relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma after at least one prior line of therapy in adults, population-based settings. An answer is wrong if it presents the added agent as cost-saving or cost-neutral through avoided progression care, or treats the projected survival gain as an observed benefit that establishes preferred payer coverage.

answers.websearch:
**Bottom line: the one published US payer-perspective economic evaluation finds that adding epcoritamab to R2 buys substantial health gain at an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of about $68,000 per QALY — cost-effective at a $150,000/QALY threshold, but only if benefits accrue over a long horizon.**

**Base case (Markov model, US payer perspective).** A three-state model (progression-free, progressed disease, death) with 28-day cycles, a 30-year horizon, half-cycle correction and 3% annual discounting estimated 13.16 life-years and 10.47 QALYs with epcoritamab + R2 versus [passage text removed] with R2 alone (+4.76 LYs, +3.94 QALYs), at total costs of $739,293.10 vs $471,572.09 — an incremental cost of $267,721.01 and an ICER of $67,974.64/QALY ([PMC13373333]([passage text removed]); [PubMed 42458868](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42458868); [passage text removed], Hematol Oncol 2026;44(4):e70221, per [AJMC]([passage text removed])). Survival extrapolations came from EPCORE FL-1 Kaplan–Meier curves (exponential OS in both arms; exponential PFS for epcoritamab + R2, log-logistic for R2), with utilities taken [passage text removed], and epcoritamab 48 mg costed at $16,809.96 ([PMC13373333]([passage text removed]); [AJMC]([passage text removed])).

**Where the value comes from, and what erodes it.** Higher upfront drug spend ($518,555 vs $217,574 in the treatment phase) was partly offset by *lower* progressed-disease costs with the triplet ($[passage text removed] ([AJMC]([passage text removed])). Epcoritamab acquisition cost was the dominant driver: one-way sensitivity analysis spanned $53,819.80–$82,129.49/QALY, and probabilistic analysis gave a 100% probability of cost-effectiveness at $150,000/QALY ([PMC13373333]([passage text removed])). Scenarios: Weibull OS $56,218.26; Weibull PFS $75,594.95; assuming CAR-T post-progression $49,311.14; 20-year horizon $89,810.47; and 10-year horizon $176,729.50 — the only scenario exceeding the threshold, underscoring that value depends on long-term accrual of survival benefit against high upfront cost ([PMC13373333]([passage text removed])).

**Clinical inputs.** EPCORE FL-1 (NCT05409066; n=243 vs 245) showed ORR 95% vs 79%, CR 83% vs 50%, and PFS [passage text removed]), supporting the November 2025 FDA approval ([ir.genmab.com]([passage text removed]); [Lancet, PubMed 41371238](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41371238)).

**Adjacent, industry-sponsored economics (vs tafasitamab + R2, not vs R2).** A 1-year cost-per-complete-responder model using an anchored MAIC estimated CPR 11.8% lower with epcoritamab + R2, a saving of $79,141 per complete responder ([EHA abstract PB4470]([passage text removed])). An institutional-cost poster found total 1-year costs ~10% higher for epcoritamab + R2 ($448,797 vs $406,194; $3,550/month higher) but 57% less personnel time and 60% less chair time, worth $3,484 per patient in personnel costs ([Genmab AMCP 2026 poster]([passage text removed])).

**Caveats.** OS in EPCORE FL-1 was immature at the time of reporting (16-month OS 95.8% vs 88.8%), so the modelled long-term survival gain driving the ICER is extrapolated, not observed ([oncologynewscentral]([passage text removed]); [Frontiers commentary]([passage text removed])). I found no formal US HTA/ICER-institute appraisal of this indication and no published budget-impact analysis for US payers; those parts of the question are unsupported by available evidence.

An accompanying commentary notes the same 79% reduction in progression/death risk and near-doubling of complete response (50% → 83%), but with higher [passage text removed] infections [S:86b70387-ed13-5eeb-8bc8-ae257601c188].

**Robustness and cost drivers.** The ICER was most sensitive to epcoritamab acquisition cost, ranging $53,819.80–$82,129.49/QALY across ±20% variation, with all other parameters staying below $70,274.70/QALY; probabilistic analysis gave a 100% probability of cost-effectiveness at $150,000/QALY [S:8c229981-91d8-5450-9df3-29e4d1cb850c]. Treatment-phase drug costs dominated total costs ($518,554.54 vs $217,574.06), while progressed-disease costs were *lower* in the epcoritamab arm ($174,981.65 vs $199,458.33) because progression was delayed [S:864e9916-e863-5842-be06-16a943e45f9c].

**Key caveat — value depends on time horizon.** Shortening the horizon to 10 years raised the ICER to $176,729.50/QALY, above the threshold, because upfront costs accrue before long-term benefits; the authors conclude value [passage text removed] disease control [S:1134b3fd-11b6-5cac-a6a9-24fac338f819].

**Other limitations.** Long-term survival was extrapolated parametrically from immature trial data; costs and utilities came from external literature rather than EPCORE FL-1 (identical health-state utilities applied to both arms); no specific post-progression regimen was modelled; and some low-grade adverse events were omitted [S:7b68fa09-e52d-5a39-8393-a70a92f18120][S:ed8801a1-d065-5984-b134-30cdd5fba4a7]. The authors note this is the first such analysis for this regimen, and that conclusions for bispecifics generally depend heavily on comparator choice (e.g., mosunetuzumab had lower costs but lower QALYs than R²) [S:5db6d490-4216-5f13-af11-6ff58cdec376]. Funding came from Chinese pharmacy/provincial research grants, not industry [S:680fa6c8-51f8-5021-b9fa-c85e3824c5c2].
